data.text: [00:06]Ok, um growing up, I used to go on holiday to a place in Northumberland called Seahouses, um and the most impressive thing about Seahouses is the miles and miles of unspoilt idyllic beaches. `[00:24]You can walk for miles and miles and only see a man and his dog and it’s fantastic. `[00:33]The biggest feeling you get when you’re there is being entirely relaxed. `[00:41]Um, it’s such a a good um contrast with the city, um and generations of my family have been going there ahm, I think it was my great great grandfather ah discovered this small seaside town ah many years ago and ever since ahm my family’s been going there and ah yeah it’s fantastic.

[01:15]One of the most beautiful places I’ve ever been to is in Southern Thailand and it’s a peninsula called Railay. `[01:23]It’s a beautiful, unspoilt lush scenery. `[01:27.9]It takes five minutes to walk from one side of the peninsula to the other. `[01:33]Erm, one of the beaches that I used to visit I had to walk through caves to get to it, ahm, and it was a hidden beach um um and when I went swimming um you can see to the bottom in about ten feet of water. `[01:50]There’s tropical fish everywhere the sun is shining and in the distance all you can see is dots of other islands in the distance. `[02:01.9]It’s very relaxing, ahm very calm very serene. It’s a very tranquil place to spend spend the afternoon.
